args.common: ROUND 2 of the water lane (started by the lead 22 Nov 18:10 WIB after the round-1 re-judge). CLIENT'S WORDS (verbatim, 22 Nov): 'cek flicker tulil.mov, ITUU GOBLOG' (desktop: blocky dark shapes along the left ice sheets' waterline reflections, much worse while the camera moves); 'gila, itu reflection yang bongkahan es belakang kek kontol banget, vertical line gitu doang anjing, kasar banget' (the far ice chunks' reflections are rough flat vertical lines); 'cek bibir air jelek.mov, bagian situ juga anjing jelek bangetttt refleksi air dan tepi bongkahan es nyaa' (the water lip and the ice edges at the far slabs). The client's videos: MAIN/flicker tulil.mov and MAIN/bibir air jelek.mov (look at them; frames: ffmpeg -ss <t> -i ... -frames:v 1). The client's machine is a base Apple M4 = tier T1 on a DPR 2 display; Safari on any Apple Silicon Mac is T1 too. Other standing words: 'please make no mistakes', 'jangan buang buang token ... efisien', awwwards site-of-the-day level. STATE AFTER ROUND 1: lane LANES/p4wl, lab :5163, is FROZEN (never edit it, never stop :5163; it is every round-2 lane's base). It added P4WL_BAND (the band-limited quarter walk, default on T1 and T2): floe-foot pops -17 to -24 % at the same poses, about +1 % T1 sweep, no regressions, all hard gates except (b) pass. Read the round-1 re-judge: MAIN/notes/round11/lane_backup/p4wl/rejudge_p4wl/LOG.md, and the round-1 HANDOFF: LANES/p4wl/HANDOFF.md. Open findings: WL-RJ1 major: in the open water right of the left shelf (CSS x ~280-480, y ~440-520 at 1440x766) the shelf's dark reflection still has a crenellated outline that takes a new shape every frame at T1 DPR 1 and 2, the same as MAIN. Only the per-pixel walk (?wlwalk=px or ?lkhalf=0) removes it; round 1 measured px at +8.7 % T1 sweep in a run with bimodal timing, and px shows pixel speckle at DPR 1. Root cause per the re-judge: each quarter tap stores point samples (horizon, face colour) of a field that jumps wherever the walk changes obstacle cell. The quarter grid lives in screen space, so it slides across the lake with every camera step and redraws the contour each frame. WL-J2 major: job B (far columns, lips) is not built; the plan is in LANES/p4wl/HANDOFF.md, section 'WL-J2 / job B plan'. TOOLS: reuse round 1's: $SP/work_p4/p4wl/tools (cap.mjs, capa.py, cmp2.py, gtpop.py [the box is 4 separate numbers], idchain2.sh, perf2.sh, perfab.mjs, finstrip.py, slabcrop.py, rl.mjs, mkvid.py, sbs.py) and the re-judge's same-pose stepped and real-loop tools in $SP/work_p4/rejudge_p4wl; the per-pixel 2x GT = ?wlwalk=px&lkmeach=1. BASELINES: :5162 = MAIN's water (LANES/p4ph); :5163 = round 1 (LANES/p4wl). THE BAR, every item on your FINAL build: (1) The morphing contour is gone at T1 DPR 1 and DPR 2 where the client looks: a same-pose sheet MAIN | p4wl | lane | px | GT of the shelf-water band shows no frame-to-frame reshaping in the lane (look at it). (2) Left-box and shelf-water-box one-frame blips within +15 % of the GT, and the far box not worse than :5163. (3) T1 pointer sweep <= +5 % vs :5162 with >= 8 interleaved STRICT pairs; report the paired median and both modes (identical code is bimodal, about 20.1 / 21.5 ms). (4) No new sparkle at 60 fps. (5) The FAIR gate on all six paths, against each build's own 16-sample GT (gt_new tools). (6) ?<your switch>=0 is IDENTICAL to :5163 and ?p4wl=0 is IDENTICAL to :5162: ident at T1, T2, T0 phone and p04 / p06 / p07. (7) The ice rings' look unchanged (the client's decision); T0 phones unchanged unless proven better; tsc clean in both configs; 0 console errors. CLIENT FILES: side-by-sides MAIN | lane at 1x and 2x, plus a short mp4 at T1 DPR 2 (MAIN left, lane right), into MAIN/notes/round11/refs_user/wl2_<lane>_*. Short dated LOG entries; delete capture sets once analysed (the disk is tight: keep < 3 GB per WORK); self-gate before ok = true. LEAD NOTE 20:30 (after the round-2 lane judges; binds the final judge, the fixer and the re-judge): judge_wl2g found WL2G-J1 major. In the REAL LOOP at T1 DPR 2 (the client's own setup), the water in front of the left ice sheets pops about 55 % more than MAIN. It is inherited from round 1's P4WL_BAND; round 1's re-judge had seen lane 1212 vs MAIN 767 blips there and called it dt-confounded. Treat the dt-controlled real loop at T1 DPR 2 as the deciding test for the client's complaint: compare equal frame-time bands, n >= 100 frames each, and look at the frames. Whatever merges must not pop more than MAIN there. If P4WL_BAND causes it, root-cause it and fix it, or drop the band share where it causes the pops while keeping wl2g's stable contour. Prove it with the real-loop numbers and a MAIN | lane strip.

wl2g.build: LANE wl2g (lab :5164): fix WL-RJ1 by ANCHORING THE WALK IN LAKE SPACE (the re-judge's option 1). Each lake point must keep its walk sample while the camera moves. Compute the walk on a grid fixed in lake xz (world) space instead of the screen-space quarter grid. For example: a lake-space walk texture whose texel footprint at the shelf band is <= the current quarter texel, read with bilinear filtering; or snap the quarter pass's reprojection to world texels. Either way the sampling grid no longer slides, and bilinear reads keep the contour smooth, not stair-stepped. Keep P4WL_BAND's share smoothing. Prefer reusing the existing quarter target budget. Switch ?wl2g=0 = :5163 exactly. Files: world/Water.ts (plus LakeMirror.ts / RenderPipeline.ts only if needed: say so); HeroEngine.ts small hunks only.
wl2g.judge: Judge lane wl2g against WL-RJ1 and THE BAR. Same-pose stepped sheets MAIN | p4wl | lane | px | GT of the shelf-water band (CSS x 280-480, y 440-520) and the left box (0-420 x 470-620) at T1 DPR 1 and 2: does the contour still reshape frame to frame (look). Blip counts vs GT; far box vs :5163; a real loop at T1 DPR 2, controlled for dt; your own perf A/B (>= 8 pairs); ident; 60 fps sparkle; FAIR on at least the fast and reverse paths; anything worse anywhere (rest look, T2, T0, hold sweep). LENSES: glitch_cursor_orbit, environment, glitch_hold_sweep, awwwards_jury.

wl2f.build: LANE wl2f (lab :5165): fix WL-RJ1 by FOOTPRINT-FILTERING WHAT EACH QUARTER TAP STORES (the re-judge's option 2). Store a footprint-filtered horizon instead of the centre ray's point sample: min / max or mean over the texel's lake footprint (for example 4 sub-rays spread over that footprint, or an analytic prefilter of the obstacle height field), and filter the face colour the same way. Then a 1-texel camera shift changes the stored value by a small, continuous amount. If the stored quarter values cannot be made continuous, fall back to the per-pixel walk on T1: (i) remove its speckle at the source by band-limiting the bump / heightfield the walk samples by its screen derivatives; (ii) cut its cost to <= +5 % T1 sweep, measured with >= 8 pairs (step count by distance, early-out, reduced rate only where the band is far). Switch ?wl2f=0 = :5163 exactly. Files: world/Water.ts; HeroEngine.ts small hunks only.
wl2f.judge: Judge lane wl2f against WL-RJ1 and THE BAR. Same-pose stepped sheets MAIN | p4wl | lane | px | GT of the shelf-water band (CSS x 280-480, y 440-520) and the left box (0-420 x 470-620) at T1 DPR 1 and 2: does the contour still reshape frame to frame (look). Blip counts vs GT; far box vs :5163; a real loop at T1 DPR 2, controlled for dt; your own perf A/B (>= 8 pairs); ident; 60 fps sparkle; FAIR on at least the fast and reverse paths; anything worse anywhere (rest look, T2, T0, hold sweep). LENSES: glitch_cursor_orbit, environment, glitch_hold_sweep, awwwards_jury.

wl2b.build: LANE wl2b (lab :5166): JOB B = WL-J2. Follow the round-1 fixer's plan (LANES/p4wl/HANDOFF.md 'WL-J2 / job B plan') and the re-judge's fix text. Measure each far slab / floe's reflection column length and peak brightness against ref_F000 (crops: the far slabs CSS ~880-1440 x 480-640 and the left slabs). Lengthen and brighten the columns toward the reference: a scale on sE for the faces' share only; check how far the walk reaches. Break the columns with the pixel's own mip-filtered lake_chop slope, so they do not read as rough flat vertical lines (the client's words), gated by far-box blips <= GT. Fix the notched water lips at the slab feet from 'bibir air jelek.mov' with a bilinear footprint height or a distance field at the slab feet: no stair-steps, no crawling notches in motion. Stay away from the walk code that the RJ1 lanes (wl2g, wl2f) change: own the far-column shading and the slab-foot lip, and say exactly which Water.ts parts you changed (the integrator merges 3-way). Switch ?wl2b=0 = :5163 exactly. Prove it with REF | lane | MAIN crops at 1x and 2x, at rest and in motion (T1 and T2), plus the column-length / brightness numbers. THE BAR items (3)-(7) apply; for (1) / (2), the left / shelf boxes must stay equal to :5163.
wl2b.judge: Judge lane wl2b against WL-J2 and the client's complaints about the far reflections and the lips: REF | lane | MAIN crops at 1x / 2x at rest and in motion (T1, T2); column length / peak brightness numbers vs ref_F000; far-box blips vs GT; the lips at the slab feet in motion (no notches, no crawl); THE BAR items (3)-(7); nothing worse elsewhere. LENSES: environment, color_grade_post, glitch_cursor_orbit, awwwards_jury.

args.integrate: INTEGRATOR: create lane LANES/wl2 as an APFS clone of LANES/p4wl (cp -c -R), lab :5167. CHOOSE THE WL-RJ1 WINNER between wl2g and wl2f, in this order: (a) a lane whose judge passed (no blocker / major / minor open) wins; (b) if both passed, the one with fewer shelf-water-box blips vs GT, then the lower T1 sweep cost; (c) if neither passed, the one whose judge found the morphing contour gone, even with other findings open, and list those findings; (d) if neither removed the contour, take neither (keep p4wl's band walk) and say so plainly. Take wl2b if its judge passed, or if its open findings are minor or nit only; otherwise leave it out and say why. MERGE the chosen lanes 3-way onto p4wl (base = LANES/p4wl). Keep each lane's switch (?wl2g=0 or ?wl2f=0, and ?wl2b=0); ?p4wl=0 must still equal :5162; all chosen switches off must equal :5163 exactly. THEN, on the merged build: tsc in both configs; ident (all switches off vs :5163, ?p4wl=0 vs :5162, each switch's own off state); the WL-RJ1 sheet and numbers; the job-B crops; a perf A/B (>= 8 pairs, T1 sweep vs :5162); the FAIR gate on all six paths; client files refs_user/wl2_merged_* (MAIN | merged at 1x / 2x, plus the mp4 at T1 DPR 2). Write the patch vs LANES/p4ph/retrux-web/app (= what would merge into MAIN). ok = false if any hard gate fails (say which).
args.final_judge: FINAL JUDGE of the merged lane wl2 (:5167). The client's three complaints decide: (1) the desktop flicker at the left ice sheets while the camera moves (T1 DPR 2 = the client's Mac; also T1 DPR 1 and T2); (2) the far ice chunks' reflections: not rough vertical lines, like ref_F000; (3) the water lip and the ice edges at the far slabs (bibir air). Use same-pose sheets MAIN | wl2 | GT, REF crops, a real loop at T1 DPR 2, perf, ident, FAIR, 60 fps sparkle, T0 phone, and check the ice look is unchanged. LENSES: environment, glitch_cursor_orbit, glitch_hold_sweep, color_grade_post, awwwards_jury.
